question: Como carregar somente duas colunas de um CSV?

claims.text: Para carregar apenas duas colunas de um CSV, você pode usar o parâmetro `usecols` com os nomes ou índices das colunas desejadas. Por exemplo: `pd.read_csv('arquivo.csv', usecols=['coluna1', 'coluna2'])` ou `pd.read_csv('arquivo.csv', usecols=[0, 1])`.

evidence_quotes.quote:
The `usecols` argument allows you to select any subset of the columns in a
file, either using the column names, position numbers or a callable:

```
In [61]: data = "a,b,c,d\n1,2,3,foo\n4,5,6,bar\n7,8,9,baz"

In [62]: pd.read_csv(StringIO(data))
Out[62]:
   a  b  c    d
0  1  2  3  foo
1  4  5  6  bar
2  7  8  9  baz

In [63]: pd.read_csv(StringIO(data), usecols=["b", "d"])
Out[63]:
   b    d
0  2  foo
1  5  bar
2  8  baz

In [64]: pd.read_csv(StringIO(data), usecols=[0, 2, 3])
Out[64]:
   a  c    d
0  1  3  foo
1  4  6  bar
2  7  9  baz

In [65]: pd.read_csv(StringIO(data), usecols=lambda x: x.upper() in ["A", "C"])
Out[65]:
   a  c
0  1  3
1  4  6
2  7  9
```

The `usecols` argument can also be used to specify which columns not to
use in the final result:

sources.title: or absolute, starting with a slash:\
sources.section: Handling “bad” lines — The callable function will handle only a line with too many fields.
sources.text:
The callable function will handle only a line with too many fields.
Bad lines caused by other errors will be silently skipped.

```
In [167]: bad_lines_func = lambda line: print(line)

In [168]: data = 'name,type\nname a,a is of type a\nname b,"b\" is of type b"'

In [169]: data
Out[169]: 'name,type\nname a,a is of type a\nname b,"b" is of type b"'

In [170]: pd.read_csv(StringIO(data), on_bad_lines=bad_lines_func, engine="python")
Out[170]:
     name            type
0  name a  a is of type a
```

The line was not processed in this case, as a “bad line” here is caused by an escape character.

You can also use the `usecols` parameter to eliminate extraneous column
data that appear in some lines but not others:

The callable function will handle only a line with too many fields.
Exemplo com exceção; pilha interna omitida.
ValueError: Usecols do not match columns, columns expected but not found: [0, 1, 2]

In case you want to keep all data including the lines with too many fields, you can
specify a sufficient number of `names`. This ensures that lines with not enough
fields are filled with `NaN`.

```
In [172]: pd.read_csv(StringIO(data), names=['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'])
Out[172]:
        a                b   c   d
0    name             type NaN NaN
1  name a   a is of type a NaN NaN
2  name b  b is of type b" NaN NaN
```
